productFlow.scenario: Review managed session history UI before production implementation.
productFlow.frequency: high for task composer, medium for session detail
productFlow.ownerSurface: Prototype Canvas and generated HTML prototype
productFlow.usabilityTask: Inspect the proposed UI, adjust layout/copy, and export the prototype for Visual QA.
productFlow.partialAcceptanceOrFollowUp: Gate 2 will import ASCII automatically; Gate 3 will add visual editing.

surfaces.name: Home Workspace

productFlow.scenario: Run or continue a managed Codex task from the home workspace.
productFlow.ownerSurface: Home task workspace with right context rail
productFlow.usabilityTask: Use Codex to run a repository task and find the latest managed session.
productFlow.partialAcceptanceOrFollowUp: Session detail opens from the context rail.

acceptanceSignals: Findable: task input and run action are visible without explanation.
Understandable: current execution state and next step are visible.
Actionable: run, cancel, continue, result, and open session actions have clear consequences.
Traceable: latest managed session is reachable without exposing raw evidence first.

regions.name: Current Task Intent

productFlow.scenario: Describe and run a local agent task.
productFlow.usabilityTask: Type a task, select computer and agent, review safety, and run.
productFlow.partialAcceptanceOrFollowUp: Advanced evidence and session detail remain outside this region.

acceptanceSignals: Findable: task input is the first control in the left column.
Understandable: safety/data/cost/cancel review is plain language.
Actionable: run and cancel are visible.
Traceable: user can continue to result/session through context rail.

elements.label: Before you run: Codex will continue the latest managed session using the selected computer and agent.

regions.name: Current Task Execution

productFlow.scenario: Watch status and result after running a task.
productFlow.usabilityTask: Understand whether the task is ready, running, waiting for approval, or complete.

acceptanceSignals: Findable: current state appears in the middle column.
Understandable: state copy uses plain language.
Actionable: approval or result actions appear only when relevant.
Traceable: result can lead to diff/session context.

regions.name: Context, History, Governance
regions.ownerSurface: Right rail: context, history, and governance

productFlow.scenario: Find latest managed session and open detail without crowding the task composer.
productFlow.usabilityTask: Continue, view result, or open the latest managed session.
productFlow.partialAcceptanceOrFollowUp: Evidence Center remains an advanced entry.

acceptanceSignals: Findable: latest managed session appears in the right rail.
Understandable: session status and counts are summarized.
Actionable: Continue, Result, and Open session are distinct.
Traceable: Evidence Center is reachable as an advanced entry.

elements.label: Repo: myagenttool; Agent: Codex CLI; Mode: Managed

surfaces.name: Session Detail

productFlow.scenario: Inspect and continue turns inside a managed Codex session.
productFlow.ownerSurface: Session detail opened from context rail
productFlow.usabilityTask: Review previous turns and add a follow-up without losing session context.
productFlow.partialAcceptanceOrFollowUp: Diff review remains a later detail flow.

acceptanceSignals: Findable: session detail opens from the right rail.
Understandable: turns are labeled as initial, follow-up, feedback, or retry.
Actionable: user can send follow-up or attach diff context.
Traceable: follow-ups reuse managed session context and evidence records.
whatNotToShow: private Codex session files as primary evidence

regions.name: Session Turns

productFlow.usabilityTask: Find prior turns and understand their status.
productFlow.partialAcceptanceOrFollowUp: Raw evidence is accessed from Evidence Center, not this list.

acceptanceSignals: Findable: turn list is visible in session detail.
Understandable: turn labels are plain language.
Actionable: user can choose next follow-up.
Traceable: each turn remains tied to managed session context.

elements.label: Initial task: Fix failing tests in the Web Console
Follow-up: Adjust result copy after reviewing the diff
Feedback: Respond to review comment about mobile wrapping

regions.name: Add Follow-up

productFlow.scenario: Send feedback or a follow-up inside an existing managed session.
productFlow.usabilityTask: Ask the next step in this session and attach diff context if needed.

acceptanceSignals: Findable: Add follow-up appears only in session detail.
Understandable: copy says the follow-up reuses managed session context.
Actionable: send follow-up and attach diff context are separate.
Traceable: follow-up creates its own evidence record.

elements.label: Ask the next step in this session
